title: P46 (Chester Beatty II): 1 Corinthians 1:4-2:2 (fols. 38v-39v)
source: P46 (Chester Beatty Biblical Papyrus II, Chester Beatty Library, Dublin): photographs as published in the INTF New Testament Virtual Manuscript Room; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P46; English from the King James Version
description: 1 Corinthians 1:4-2:2 in P46, the papyrus codex of Paul's letters copied around 200: fols. 38v-39v, each page with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P46 is a papyrus codex of the letters of Paul copied in Egypt around 200, the oldest surviving collection of Paul's letters. 86 of its 104 leaves survive: 56 in the Chester Beatty Library, Dublin (Biblical Papyrus II, published by Frederic Kenyon in 1934-1937) and 30 in the University of Michigan Library, Ann Arbor (P.Mich. inv. 6238, published by Henry Sanders in 1935). The letters run in the order Romans, Hebrews, 1 and 2 Corinthians, Ephesians, Galatians, Philippians, Colossians and 1 Thessalonians; the first seven leaves (Romans 1:1-5:17) and the end of the book are lost. Hebrews standing after Romans, and the doxology of Romans (16:25-27) standing after 15:33, are among its best-known features.

Each section below is one page side: the holding library's photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription line by line, and the King James Version of every verse that has text on the page. The lower lines of many leaves are lost; the transcribers' restorations are in square brackets.

This entry covers fols. 38v-39v (1 Corinthians 1:4-2:2).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>1:4</sup>I thank my God always on your behalf, for the grace of God which is given you by Jesus Christ; <sup>5</sup>That in every thing ye are enriched by him, in all utterance, and in all knowledge; <sup>6</sup>Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you: <sup>7</sup>So that ye come behind in no gift; waiting for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ: <sup>8</sup>Who shall also confirm you unto the end, that ye may be blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. <sup>9</sup>God is faithful, by whom ye were called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord. <sup>10</sup>Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment. <sup>11</sup>For it hath been declared unto me of you, my brethren, by them which are of the house of Chloe, that there are contentions among you. <sup>12</sup>Now this I say, that every one of you saith, I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ. <sup>13</sup>Is Christ divided? was Paul crucified for you? or were ye baptized in the name of Paul? <sup>14</sup>I thank God that I baptized none of you, but Crispus and Gaius;
translation.scan_note: Chester Beatty Library photograph T0005496.jpg (https://ntmss.info/images/webfriendly/10046/T0005496.jpg), linked to NTVMR page 580 (folio 38v) in NTVMR's page index. 1:4 begins on the previous page; 1:14 continues on the next page. Checked on the image: the scribe's page number οε (75) at the head of the page, continuing the sequence of the neighbouring pages.

translation.text: <sup>1:14</sup>I thank God that I baptized none of you, but Crispus and Gaius; <sup>15</sup>Lest any should say that I had baptized in mine own name. <sup>16</sup>And I baptized also the household of Stephanas: besides, I know not whether I baptized any other. <sup>17</sup>For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel: not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect. <sup>18</sup>For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God. <sup>19</sup>For it is written, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent. <sup>20</sup>Where is the wise? where is the scribe? where is the disputer of this world? hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world? <sup>21</sup>For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. <sup>22</sup>For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom: <sup>23</sup>But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Greeks foolishness;

Checked on the image: the scribe's page number ος (76) at the head of the page, continuing the sequence of the neighbouring pages; the disc on the frame reads ‹P. II 39R›.

translation.text: <sup>1:24</sup>But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God. <sup>25</sup>Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men. <sup>26</sup>For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called: <sup>27</sup>But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; <sup>28</sup>And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: <sup>29</sup>That no flesh should glory in his presence. <sup>30</sup>But of him are ye in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption: <sup>31</sup>That, according as it is written, He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord. <sup>2:1</sup>And I, brethren, when I came to you, came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom, declaring unto you the testimony of God. <sup>2</sup>For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
